findings.title: Error events are paired by dict order and compared with the wrong timestamp type
findings.body: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore get_multi().values(). If the backend omits missing keys or does not return results in request order, titles/messages are attached to the wrong event ids (or dropped while a later id is kept). It also stores data.get("timestamp") as-is. Nodestore events normally have an ISO string timestamp, while breadcrumb timestamps in gen_request_data are numbers. Sorting and the `<` comparison then raise TypeError and the summarize endpoint 500s whenever error context is enabled. The new tests only cover events stored with a numeric timestamp, so they miss production nodestore payloads.

findings.title: Assemble analytics runs before the feature gate and assumes a real user
findings.body: analytics.record is called with user_id=request.user.id before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble check and before auth-token handling. This endpoint is used by org auth tokens (is_org_auth_token_auth later in the same method). AnonymousUser has no id, so request.user.id raises AttributeError and the assemble API 500s for the token clients it is meant to serve. The event is also recorded for requests that will immediately 404 because the feature is off.

findings.title: Flagged table widgets render empty data instead of query results
findings.body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, tableResultComponent ignores result.data, result.meta, fields, and field renderers and mounts TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData data: []. Dashboards with that flag show a blank table even when the widget query succeeded. The previous StyledSimpleTableChart path, which actually binds the query result, is skipped entirely.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
findings.body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the search filter. The empty-query branch returns sortAttributes(attributes) unchanged, so those fields still render in the default Attributes tree. They disappear only after the user types a search string, which is the opposite of hiding them.

findings.title: Saved-search conversion is no-op'd with no replacement migration
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 now return immediately, and tests/sentry/migrations/test_0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py is deleted. The comment points at 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, but that migration is not in this PR. Environments that have not yet applied 0917/0920 will never copy organization SavedSearch rows into GroupSearchView, and nothing in this change still tests that conversion.
